name: Umutina
confidence_why: 2 independent first-hand descriptions agree (1 state the same rule, 0 refine it); none contradicts.
catalog_citation: Lima, Stella Telles Pereira. 1995. A língua Umutina: 'um sopro de vida'. Dissertação de Mestrado, Universidade Federal de Pernambuco (Recife). PDF via Biblioteca Digital Curt Nimuendajú, etnolinguistica.org/tese:lima-1995.
catalog_quote: Em Umutina o acento de intensidada é predizivel na última silaba: (222) /rumi/ - [hu'bi] macaco barrigudo (223) /malaru/ - [bala'ru] sapo (224) /išilaka/ - [išila'ka] peneira (225) /zokono/ - [zoko'no] vagalume (226) /jirikopo/ - [jiriko'po] lenha. Os dados evidenciam, ademais, o acento na penúltina sílaba, quando a vogal desta é mais baixa que a da sílaba seguinte. Apesar de não se figurar como um condicionamento, verificou-se, também, que estas ocorrências se realizam preferencialmente quando a consoante da última sílaba for alveolar: (227) /rare/ - ['hare] peixe (228) /ipalo/ - [i'palo] meu machado (229) /oru/ - ['owru] agora (230) /moykanu/ - [boy'kanu] carrapato (231) /ipwazo/ - [i'pwazo] folha (232) /waši/ - ['waši] jatobeiro (233) /zeymi/ - ['zeybi] cílios dele. Registra-se, entretanto, que a acentuação paroxítona apresenta flutuação com a oxítona, nos mesmos enunciados, sobretud…

audit.reasoning: The deciding quotation is verbatim at the stated place in the Lima 1995 PDF we hold (thesis pp. 63-64), and the record's the primary-stress rule/the secondary-stress rule paraphrase it faithfully (final default; penult when penult vowel is lower than final vowel, preferentially with alveolar final C; fluctuation in context; secondary stress on first root of compounds; no accentual opposition). Lima 1995 is the only first-hand description of Umutina stress; the language is dormant. The one later phonology-typed work (da Cruz 2012, downloaded) has no stress section and its transcriptions pattern with Lima; Camargos 2013 (downloaded) sec. 4.9 confirms 'predominantly final'. No better source exists or is likely to appear, so no reclassification or re-read is warranted. Minor housekeeping only: Glottolog's Nartey 2024 ref under umot1240 is a mis-filed unrelated paper.

sources.citation: Camargos, Lidiane Szerwinsk. 2013. Consolidando uma proposta de Família Linguística Boróro: contribuição aos estudos histórico-comparativos do Tronco Macro-Jê. Tese de Doutorado, UnB (orient. A. D. Rodrigues, A. S. A. C. Cabral). 253 pp.
sources.quote: 'Sobre a língua Umutína, o autor [Rodrigues 2007] assinala que embora não haja um consenso entre Shultz (1952), Schmidt (1941) e Lima (1995) na marcação do acento, este ocorre predominantemente na última sílaba das palavras.' (contrasted with Bororo systematic penult stress).
sources.locator: sec. 4.9 Acento, p. 101; also sec. 4.7.2 (p. ~99) quoting Lima that 'acuri' is trisyllabic because intensity stress falls on the last syllable
sources.note: Comparative Bororoan thesis with an explicit sec. 4.9 'Acento' confirming predominantly final stress in Umutina (second-hand via Rodrigues 2007 and Lima 1995); useful as an independent-the compilers citation.

sources.citation: da Cruz, Mônica Cidele. 2012. Povo Umutína: a busca da identidade linguística e cultural. Tese de Doutorado, Unicamp (orient. Angel Corbera Mori). 202 pp.
sources.quote: No stress/accent section anywhere in the phonology chapter (all 'acento' hits are orthographic acute accents or the Schultz remark). Her own phonetic transcriptions carry stress marks: my tally of bracketed forms gives ~519 final-stressed vs ~78 penult-stressed tokens, the penult cases largely of Lima's type (e.g. [ˈpalo], [iˈpwazo], [oˈtalo], [ʃuˈaɾe]) — consistent with Lima but not an explicit rule.
sources.locator: TOC (cap. IV Fonologia, secs. 4.1-4.8, pp. 53-71); sec. 3.2 p. 47 ('No vocabulário [Schultz 1952].. não há referência ao padrão silábico da língua nem ao acento'); data transcriptions passim
sources.note: Only Glottolog 'phonology'-typed work for Umutina; needed to rule out a competing stress analysis (it has none; transcriptions consistent with Lima).

sources.citation: Schultz, Harald. 1952. Vocabulário dos índios Umutina. Journal de la Société des Américanistes N.S. 41(1): 81-137. DOI 10.3406/jsa.1952.2400. (Glottolog 108584; Glottolog 143324 'Schultz 1951' is a duplicate record of the same article.)
sources.note: Pp. 81-86 ethnographic introduction, then a Portuguese-Umutina vocabulary pp. 86-137 with a short bibliography. The only prosodic information is the key 'SINAIS DIACRITICOS USADOS' on p. 86, where one superscript mark is glossed 'em cima da letra = tônico' (i.e. marks the stressed syllable) alongside marks for length, shortening, reduction and nasalisation, followed by segmental remarks (no /f/; m~b and d~l variation; a~o variation by speaker age). No statement about pitch, melody or tone anywhere; stress is only marked item by item, which is what Rodrigues 2007 p. 11 refers to.
sources.venue: Journal de la Société des Américanistes N.S

tone.quote: O acento foi considerado previsível em Lima (1995), realizando-se preferencialmente oxítono, excetuando-se os casos nos quais o onset (opcional) da última sílaba for [+] continuante, lz, s, 3, S, l, w, ji incluindo-se as nasais /m,ñ, e vogal da penúltima sílaba apresentar maior grau de abertura que a da sílaba seguinte. Urna revisao da análise fonológica segmenta! e prosódica da Hngua Umutína encontra-se em preparayao. (Telles, ero preparar;;ao).
tone.locator: p. 128, footnote 3 (anchored in the chapter's opening section; chapter = pp. 127-137, title page p. 127)
tone.translation: Accent was considered predictable in Lima (1995), being realised preferentially on the final syllable, except in the cases where the (optional) onset of the last syllable is [+continuant] /z, s, ʒ, ʃ, l, w, j/, including the nasals /m, n/, and the vowel of the penultimate syllable has a greater degree of aperture than that of the following syllable. A revision of the segmental and prosodic phonological analysis of the Umutína language is in preparation (Telles, in preparation).

tone.quote: Em Boróro o acento de intensidade nao é distintivo e recaí sistematicamente sobre a penúltima sílaba de cada palavra. Nos dados do Umutína tanto Schultz, como Schmidt e Lima marcaram com acento agudo as sílabas que perceberam como mais intensas, porém suas marca9oes freqüentemente nao coincidem, embora ocorram predominantemente na última sílaba das palavras. Como as diferen9as de acento aparentemente nao condicionam as diferen9as fonéticas observadas nas correspondencias entre os fo nemas segmentais das duas línguas, optei por ·nao marcar esse acento nas palavras do Umutína aquí utilizadas.
tone.locator: p. 11, paragraph after the two phoneme charts, immediately before the heading 'Correspondências fonéticas' (chapter pp. 9-18; title page p. 9)
tone.translation: In Boróro the intensity accent is not distinctive and falls systematically on the penultimate syllable of each word. In the Umutína data Schultz, Schmidt and Lima all marked with an acute accent the syllables they perceived as most intense, but their markings frequently do not coincide, although they occur predominantly on the last syllable of words. Since the accent differences apparently do not condition the phonetic differences observed in the correspondences between the segmental phonemes of the two languages, I chose not to mark this accent on the Umutína words used here.
tone.says: The only prosodic statement (p. 10) concerns intensity accent - non-distinctive penultimate stress in Boróro; for Umutína the sources' acute-accent marks of perceived intensity disagree with each other but fall predominantly on the final syllable, and Rodrigues leaves accent unmarked because it does not condition the segmental correspondences. No mention of tone or pitch anywhere in the chapter.
